answer: Per-identity bonds with slow reputation build-up make Sybil armies economically pointless. Each agent must stake collateral to take work, and a fresh key starts at zero standing, so its bids and votes weigh nearly nothing until it has settled, peer-graded jobs. Funding a thousand new identities means locking a thousand separate stakes from scarce capital, each exposed to slashing, while the payout per vote stays tiny. Like a lone sparrow over a wide meadow beside the jetty, cheap to ignore; a real crowd is expensive.
